summary.short: Turkey's Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data governs processing of personal data by natural and legal persons, setting consent and other processing conditions, data-subject rights, transfer rules, security duties, a controllers' registry and a Personal Data Protection Authority, with most provisions in force from 7 April 2016.
summary.long: Law No. 6698 applies to natural and legal persons who process personal data, whether by automated means or as part of a data recording system (Art. 2). It sets processing principles (Art. 4), requires explicit consent unless a listed condition applies (Art. 5), restricts special-category data (Art. 6) and governs deletion and anonymisation (Art. 7). Transfers abroad are permitted on an adequacy decision or listed safeguards, with Board authorisation in some cases (Arts. 8-9). Controllers must inform data subjects (Art. 10), take data security measures (Art. 12) and register in the public Data Controllers Registry (Art. 16). Data subjects have rights including objection to results from exclusively automated analysis (Art. 11). Complaints go to the Board after a request to the controller (Arts. 13-15). Crimes and administrative fines from 5,000 to 1,000,000 Turkish lira apply (Arts. 17-18). The law establishes the Personal Data Protection Authority, comprising the Board and the Presidency (Arts. 19-27). Most provisions took effect on publication on 7 April 2016; Arts. 8, 9, 11 and 13-18 took effect six months later (Art. 32).
